scope_note: Names and definitions identify the programme and development scope. They do not establish a completed game, validated model, biological or clinical capability.
release_policy: Work is published here while it is still experimental, with its version, sources and limits stated. Privacy, redistribution rights, security and an honest statement of scientific scope are required of everything published.
license_note: Project-owned contributions CC0-1.0; third-party materials retain their own rights and notices.
development_status: active; work has resumed alongside NeuroSurge and Interoceptomics
programme_focus: NeuroTranslation, NeuroSurge and Interoceptomics are active together.

data_companion.version: Recording readers including first-use optical forecasts and next recorded spike prediction
data_companion.meaning: Import and inspect recordings locally. Replay the fit made on first recordings (R1), or compare the fixed and personally calibrated models on an imported second recording (R2). Complete R2 trials are checked against their archived sample clock and the four input streams the study used. Group results are shown separately.
data_companion.hosting: Static files in docs/ on the main branch, served by GitHub Pages.

navigation_overlay.scope: The recording-source chooser is part of the app. The general CSV and JSON inspector remains available.
navigation_overlay.source_count_scope: Seven recording-reader choices in the app. Two use the CEMHSEY pinch recordings for different studies.

papers.scope: The current edition, 21 November 2026: NeuroTranslation (54 pages, Simple English Edition 64) and Brain2Body (29 pages, Simple English Edition 33), working drafts not reviewed outside the project. NeuroTranslation reports every study of the numbered table, 1 to 29, with a row for each in its appendix B.
papers.build_provenance: Four PDFs built offline with the Tectonic 0.17 TeX engine; a rebuild from the source ZIP gives the same bytes.
papers.source_status: The complete source of the four PDFs (91 files: TeX, bibliography, figure, fonts and tools), the build script, and the ledger and small result files its number check reads. The TeX engine and its package files are named in the ZIP, not included.
papers.publication_scope: This block identifies the files of the current edition.

NeuroTranslation reports every study of the numbered table, 1 to 29, with a row for each in its appendix B.

selected_manuscript_source.scope: The complete source of the four PDFs (91 files: TeX, bibliography, figure, fonts and tools), the build script, and the ledger and small result files its number check reads. The TeX engine and its package files are named in the ZIP, not included.

historical_scientific_layout.scope: The 15 November 2026 edition: four drafts, 546 pages, of which 26 had a recorded visual check. The current edition replaced it; the link shows it in the repository history.
historical_scientific_layout.build_provenance: The two technical PDFs came from the previous build; the two Simple English PDFs were rebuilt, and the rebuilt Brain2Body one was byte-identical to its predecessor.

download_bundle.scope: Four PDFs, three companion files, README, manifest and five notice files; no font, source or model files.

historical_scientific_layout.source_status: No matching source was published with that edition.

portable_interface.status: Source only: no model weights, no download, nothing that runs, not a finished interface.

wrist_pointing.source_rights: CC BY 4.0, attribution included in each benchmark.
wrist_pointing.cohort_scope: Six training, three development participants; 1,879 eligible training trials and 960 eligible development trials, with six reserved participants.
wrist_pointing.scope_note: The interactive controls change explicitly invented features. Reported errors describe separate, fixed analyses of the measured pointing task at a nominal 250 ms forecast horizon; physical latency is unmeasured.

wrist_pointing_forecasts.comparison_scope: Six training participants with 1,879 eligible recorded trials; three different development participants supplied 960 complete trials. 250 ms forecast horizon on the archive clock. The reserved test recordings remain unopened.

recorded_trial_replay.verification_scope: Fingerprints cover all six input windows, measured two-axis targets, archive and clock metadata for all 960 original development trials. Six trained temporal checkpoints execute in the browser. Cohort errors and individual recorded trials have separate views. The 250 ms lead refers to stored rows; device delays are unverified.
recorded_trial_replay.public_contents: Public artifact contains aggregate scores, fitted models, code and checksums; the reader supplies a trial locally.
recorded_trial_replay.limits: Verified on Linux Chromium with hosted, offline and emulated narrow-screen cases. No recordings from the reserved test group are included or were examined.

wrist_forearm_transfer.scope: Six training participants, three previously evaluated development participants, six reserved test participants not examined.

uji_forearm_emg.scope: Offline healthy-volunteer daily activities. Participant-specific reference posture, retrospectively filtered wrist-angle targets. Observations from the four final test volunteers were not evaluated.

daily_wrist_browser.scope: Estimates of retrospectively filtered glove angles in offline daily-activity trials. The interface runs two fixed estimators and a weighted combination on invented or compatible local inputs. The weights were chosen using training data only. The four development participants had been studied before, and the final test participants are still unopened.

way_grip_force.scope: Offline voluntary pinch-lift force forecasting. Aligned scalp EEG slightly reduced equal-person development RMSE versus mechanical history. The phase-matched EEG model did better than aligned EEG.

browser.input_scope: Original single windows, invented trial replay, and compatible locally converted WAY-EEG-GAL WS trials. Four displayed predictors use preceding sensor samples. Twenty-nine separately stored later grip forces can be revealed to score each forecast. The browser ZIP contains no participant samples.

way_contact_force.scope: Two offline grip-force forecasts compared after the tenth consecutive sample at or above 0.5 N on the 500 Hz recording clock. Adding aligned scalp EEG increased average error in both families on the same development group, which had been looked at before. The final test group is still unopened. The launchers use invented input by default.

browser.scope: Fixed ridge and causal CNN weights run on the same prior window. An invented example or compatible local JSON supplies inputs. A future target sample can be shown only when supplied. Rotation is an aggregate control. The 120 ms horizon is on the recording clock.

browser.trial_replay: One right-hand trial per local file; 205 scheduled cutoffs, conditional on complete input and target support. The example is invented.
browser.signal_plot: Twenty 50 Hz transducer readings and a selectable forecast at +120 ms. Trial outcomes are shown only when revealed.

hygrip_force.scope: First scoring of three original HYGRIP development participants after public protocol posting. The browser uses fixed fits from the training group and invented example inputs by default. The final test group is still unopened.

secondary_emg.tested_endpoint: forecast of released sensor voltage 120 ms after issue
secondary_emg.scope: Secondary right-hand analysis on the same three previously studied development people. Timing-specific forearm EMG and scalp EEG directional screens failed on the training group and on the development group.

study.scope: Index-finger sensor voltage on a distinct two-day isometric task. Physical real-time lead remains unverified.
study.decision: Aligned EMG gave no average gain on the main measure in this experiment; results for each held-out participant and each day are reported.

hyser_index.scope: Released index transducer voltage 120 ms ahead on the nominal stream. Four final participants reserved. No online or clinical claim.

crossday_study.scope: Matched Day 1 supervised calibration on an output offset and gain, followed by fixed Day 2 scoring. Shared model had the lowest mean Day 2 MAE on the four development participants, who had been studied before. Paired-donor control and pair-level descriptive uncertainty are reported.

hyser_index.personal_reader: Two original same-person session folders, five labeled first-day trials, fixed second-day inference. Population mode remains available.

whole_hand.scope: Five force sensors, four prespecified fits including one other-trial control, and three same-trial predictors. MAE favored different models in the 12-person training comparison and four previously studied development participants. Reserved final participants remain unopened.

prescribed_task.scope: Unchanged Random-task weights scored on 360 prescribed N-DoF trials in 12 original fit participants and 120 in four previously evaluated development participants. Across all combinations, persistence gave lowest MAE and five histories lowest RMSE in each group. No refits. Original final participants remain excluded.

cemhsey_pinch.scope: Offline normalized scalar P200 pinch-force recording. Three fit participants over two days, four different evaluation participants on different indexed days. The public reader includes an invented model and supports local fit import; the study fit stays private. No cross-device physical availability or individual finger force inference.

cemhsey_intervals.status: Measured comparison of pooled and cue-phase widths on held-out trials; the public single-trial example uses invented values.

cemhsey_original_browser.support: Duplicate CEMHSEY GRASP Session 5 Task 2 recordings are detected from the decoded contents of the local files. Training, interval calibration and evaluation use separate recordings.

cemhsey_force_transfer.status: Second-repeat evaluation independently reproduced across three targets.
cemhsey_force_transfer.limitations: Four previously studied adults, one indexed day, fixed repeat order and nominal timing; public examples and bundled weights are invented.

cemhsey_day_transfer.status: Second repeats on the next indexed day, scored independently; the set of source recordings was checked.
cemhsey_day_transfer.limitations: One pair of indexed days, four previously studied participants, one prescribed task and nominal 120 ms timing. Public reader uses invented signals and weights by default.

cemhsey_population_phase.status: Six test records scored on an independent group, then independently reproduced. Public ranges rounded outward under the reporting rule set before the results were seen.
cemhsey_population_phase.limitations: Three fitting and three separate evaluation participants; one target on one indexed day. Other records from these people were known in prior studies. Forecast horizon uses nominal indices.

hygrip_force.status: Finished. The three development participants were first scored after the protocol was published; the results are in experimental_previews.hygrip_force. The final test group is still unopened.
hygrip_force.scope: Cued right-hand power grip in a separate dataset. Target is a transducer-voltage reading 120 ms ahead on the released clock.

hygrip_cue_phase.scope: Comparison of cue-conditioned and shared voltage dynamics on the previously studied healthy HYGRIP cohort.
hygrip_cue_phase.outcome: The phase-conditioned residual did not beat the original full-history benchmark on either split. Previously studied development cohort. The full-history ridge stays the chosen model.

hyser_index.scope: Index-finger sensor voltage on a distinct two-day isometric task. Physical real-time lead remains unverified.
hyser_index.decision: Aligned EMG gave no average gain on the main measure in this experiment; results for each held-out participant and each day are reported.

hyser_crossday.scope: Matched Day 1 supervised calibration on an output offset and gain, followed by fixed Day 2 scoring. Shared model had the lowest mean Day 2 MAE on the four development participants, who had been studied before. Paired-donor control and pair-level descriptive uncertainty are reported.

hyser_whole_hand.scope: Five force sensors, four prespecified fits including one other-trial control, and three same-trial predictors. MAE favored different models in the 12-person training comparison and four previously studied development participants. Reserved final participants remain unopened.

hyser_prescribed.scope: Unchanged Random-task weights scored on 360 prescribed N-DoF trials in 12 original fit participants and 120 in four previously evaluated development participants. Across all combinations, persistence gave lowest MAE and five histories lowest RMSE in each group. No refits. Original final participants remain excluded.

cemhsey_pinch.scope: Offline normalized scalar P200 pinch-force recording. Three fit participants over two days, four different evaluation participants on different indexed days. The public reader includes an invented model and supports local fit import; the study fit stays private. No cross-device physical availability or individual finger force inference.

cemhsey_intervals.status: Measured comparison of pooled and cue-phase widths on held-out trials; the public single-trial example uses invented values.

cemhsey_force_transfer.status: Second-repeat evaluation independently reproduced across three targets.
cemhsey_force_transfer.limitations: Four previously studied adults, one indexed day, fixed repeat order and nominal timing; public examples and bundled weights are invented.

cemhsey_day_transfer.status: Second repeats on the next indexed day, scored independently; the set of source recordings was checked.
cemhsey_day_transfer.limitations: One pair of indexed days, four previously studied participants, one prescribed task and nominal 120 ms timing. Public reader uses invented signals and weights by default.

cemhsey_population_phase.status: Six test records scored on an independent group, then independently reproduced. Public ranges rounded outward under the reporting rule set before the results were seen.
cemhsey_population_phase.limitations: Three fitting and three separate evaluation participants; one target on one indexed day. Other records from these people were known in prior studies. Forecast horizon uses nominal indices.

prospective_studies_note: Studies entered here when they were planned. All eleven now have results, given or linked in each entry; none is still waiting to be run.

calibrated_fingers_and_knee_moments.scope: Five participants with different cortical recording layouts contributed to calibrated finger-transfer comparisons. Seven walkers fitted and three tested the knee-moment model. The two studies use separate people, clocks and units.

overground_walking_force.scope: Retrospective tests on slow overground walking. Eight held-out people contributed 17 trials to the two-plate task and 16 to the assigned right-plate task. Neither established the prespecified benefit of adding muscle signals.

walking_marker_displacement.domain: Slow barefoot overground walking. The six-point and single-point studies estimate 200 ms displacement on the processed recording clock. Displayed examples are invented. The separate Interoceptomics reference shows movement observed in recordings.

cued_right_arm.domain: Supported right-arm execution in three runs from one participant. The seven-cue experiment estimates changes at the elbow, forearm and index finger. The two-cue experiment tests what scalp measurements add to an elbow forecast. The sensor readings use their native scales.

arm_transfer.domain: Supported right-arm movement after one of seven visual cues, first three execution runs from seven fitting and five assessment participants at one site. Targets are changes in three uncalibrated instrument readings.

scalp_forecast.domain: Supported right-arm movement after a visual cue at one site. Three early movement channels, six scalp electrodes and three eye measurements. Seven people supplied three fitting runs each. Five other people supplied their fourth run for assessment. Outcomes are changes in three uncalibrated instrument readings.

cervical_forecast.domain: Offline forecast of SC6 surface voltage relative to TH6 after a left median-nerve stimulus. Four development people and six assessment people in one study. The recordings do not resolve biological origin or movement.

back_rotation.domain: Unsigned change in orientation of one back-mounted sensor over 100 milliseconds in standing and walking. Four people supplied fitting trials. Of four new people, three had verifiable orientation rows. Both planned four-person tests are incomplete. Two trials per person. The source of electrical activity at the skin is unresolved.

muscle_tracking.domain: Signed change in the image-tracked length of a tibialis anterior fascicle over ten original tracker steps during seated ankle dorsiflexion. The native tracking grids vary, and the elapsed time for ten steps is unverified. Both length and pennation are estimates from a two-dimensional image.

pedal_load.domain: Seated isometric dorsiflexion with a fixed pedal. Signed change in the right load-cell channel over 100 acquisition rows, nominally 100 ms. Readings retain native conditioner units. The filename categories encode the instructed pedal setting. Individual joint angles and force calibration are unverified.

heel_and_force.domain: Right heel skin-marker displacement in laboratory XYZ millimetres and mean upward plate force in newtons over 15 samples centred 100 ms later. Barefoot C2 walking condition. Historical assessment: 53 windows from eight people. Later assessment: 31 windows from six of those people. Offline filtered recordings.

walking_instructions.domain: Two walking instructions, pelvis and right heel surface markers, 100 ms displacement from 200 ms of offline processed movement. Development used 30 participants, 180 walks and 645 eligible windows. Historical assessment used ten people, 60 walks and 216 windows. No recorded neural activity or word timing.

visual_balance.domain: Forecast head and sacrum displacement 125 ms ahead on stored, offline-processed visual-rotation walking trials. Development retained 2,430 rotations from 17 of 18 selected participants. Assessment retained 880 of 894 rotations from six people. Six reserve EEG SET/FDT recordings remained unopened. The Transformer and shared encoder each missed the adjusted scalp-benefit criterion at both markers.

muscle_motion.domain: From 625 ms of offline-processed leg voltages and sacrum motion, predict eight muscle RMS amplitudes and 32 XYZ path positions over the next 125 ms. Eighteen people provided 5,179 eligible development rotations. Six people outside training provided 879 standing and 880 walking assessment rotations. Their walking records appeared in earlier research. Six reserve participants’ recording payloads stayed unopened. The joint Transformer missed its two-outcome improvement criterion against separately trained specialists. Neither force nor neural conduction time was measured.

cross_limb_movement.domain: Across 882 lifts from three people, the shared model missed the wrist path by 4.870 mm. The arm specialist missed by 5.100 mm after the same number of arm updates and 4.394 mm when given the shared model’s full training budget. Across 1,759 visual rotations from six other people, the shared model missed the sacrum path by 2.169 mm and the exposure-matched balance specialist by 1.962 mm. The two studies measured different people performing different tasks. The arm electrical amplitude stays in its original exported units. No strict five-channel arm assessment was available.

cross_limb_path_maps.question: Does assigning an output map to each study improve movement forecasts compared with blending two maps over time?
cross_limb_path_maps.scope: Three development seeds and person-held predictions from the same two studies. Separate and time-blended output maps have 3,975 parameters each. Three wrist and six balance reserve participants were outside the comparison.

scalp_muscle_movement.question: Does scalp electrical activity improve a 125 ms forecast of muscle signal size and marker movement beyond task, recent motion, muscle history and the available electrode sites?
scalp_muscle_movement.interpretation: The central scalp branch lowered balance muscle error by 0.01435 microvolts against its reference. That comparison against a different trial from the same person gave no clear difference. Average path error increased by 0.03172 mm at the pelvis and 0.21449 mm at the wrist. These offline development recordings do not establish a neural source or an operating feedback system.

muscle_spindle.scope: Archived passive muscle and axon recording in rats. The two three-prefix evaluations were unavailable. Exploratory held-afferent fits used 3 fibers from one filename group, 94 trials and 16,262 20-ms targets. Mean count deviance favored spike history over the combined Transformer. Timely mechanics improved the combined forecast against time-shifted mechanics on its eligible subset. File-specific force/position calibration and animal-independent generalization remain unverified.

cortical_reach.scope: One macaque session, 540 rewarded originals split 324/108/108 in chronological order. Across 778 matching windows from 105 later trials, earlier sorted spikes increased joint Transformer endpoint error by 0.1070 cm. Correct vs wrong-trial timing remained unresolved. Two 3D landmarks helped during perturbations but slightly worsened reach forecasts. The archived kinematics were processed offline.

contact_forecast.scope: 26 shared electrode contacts in one macaque on September 12–13, 2017. In 2436 matched pre-target push windows from 609 second-day originals, correct movement outperformed earlier-trial movement on count deviance. The comparison to past counts and cues remained unresolved. Recorded event counts do not establish individual cell identities across dates.

target_reach.scope: People carried a cylinder to nine visual targets in separate left- and right-hand sessions. Seven people were held out. At the 15 mm crossing clock the full model missed the optical centroid by 12.13 mm at 600 ms. The benefit over pose alone remained unresolved. Recorded-frame timing is distinct from acoustic go or physical lift onset.

cylinder_rotation.scope: The one-clock sensor forecasts mean angular velocity and acceleration in the next 100 ms of later target repetitions in 24 previously recorded volunteers. Correctly paired acceleration beat an earlier-trial replacement, while improvement over angular history and cues remained uncertain. The lowest angular-velocity miss came from both sensors without target number. On-device orientation is a secondary reference.

reach_feedback.scope: One recording of one macaque. Two workspaces were interleaved. Earlier spikes improved the hand forecast and worsened the elbow forecast in the second workspace. Adding forecast motion to direct history did not improve prediction of subsequent spikes under the paired criteria.

reach_feedback_week.scope: One macaque trained on September 7 and tested on September 14. The two held blocks share 37 contacts with a represented sort-zero class and 17 with positive sorted units. The anatomy readout concerns OpenSim path lengths derived from tracking.

human_wrist_cross_day.scope: One person, two recordings, one pair of wrists at camera-frame horizons of eight and fifteen. Events are retrospective right-wrist movements. The public demonstration is simulated; compatible recordings and trained fits can be prepared and opened locally.

cross_person_wrist.scope: One person supplied the right-wrist reaches for fitting. A different person supplied the left-wrist reaches for testing. Both wrists were scored from camera-derived positions. The distributed tracks and fitted weights are synthetic.

next_neuron_prediction.meaning: Predict which of the recorded neurons fires the next spike using only earlier activity.
next_neuron_prediction.status: Implemented and evaluated on sorted spike histories from two rats in the same laboratory and task, with a frozen fit transferred between local unit sets.
next_neuron_prediction.correction: The selected source scorer includes exact closing boundaries. The refit coefficients and both held score files reproduced.

unfamiliar_bodies.unit_of_evaluation: Group by biological individual, recording and acquisition site as applicable. For neural generalization, evaluate diverse vertebrate clades and classes, recording types, tasks, individuals and sites. The optical landmark study separately compares animal movement in the camera plane.
unfamiliar_bodies.optional_invertebrate_evidence: Invertebrate recordings are optional. To test their value, train otherwise matched models with and without them, then compare their predictions on the same held-out vertebrates.

vertebrate_neural_data.scope: The register counts source deposits. The original two-rat study and the separate turtle dorsal cortex and salamander retina tests use recorded spike times and local unit labels. Neither the deposit count nor these three experiments measures general transfer across vertebrates.

neural_and_muscle_composites.reach: One macaque, one later day, two sensors, two horizons, three architectures and prespecified baselines.
neural_and_muscle_composites.balance: Surface EMG and sacrum motion in six historically examined held participants. No learned grouping won on both targets.
neural_and_muscle_composites.geometry: Adding modelled muscle–tendon lengths did not improve the handle endpoint forecast in both workspaces.

neurotranslate_joint_alpha.domain: Seven heads and one jointly trained temporal encoder. Earlier input and output measurements are paired only within their original recording. Eleven retrospective comparisons include five with lower primary error than the matched single-task models and six with higher error.
